dialogues.speaker: Timmie
dialogues.text: I won, I won!

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: Thanks. I can't wait to tell my mom... this'll make her really happy, won't it?

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: Mom was the one who kept telling me I should join the tournament, so I'm gonna give the prizes to her!

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: I really wish my dad could see me now...

response.speaker: Timmie
response.text: Bye! Ah, Genius Invokation is sooo much fun...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Wait, why's everyone leaving? ...Did I miss it...?

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Ah Mika, too bad you weren't here to see it. I'm afraid that... Captain Kaeya lost.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Tell me everything! What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Well, I don't know much about Genius Invokation myself, but I did try to follow along by listening in to what everyone was saying...

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Captain Kaeya took out one of Timmie's character cards right at the start, giving him an early advantage.

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: But I guess that was all part of his opponent's strategy...? In any case, Timmie spent the first few rounds stocking up cards in his hand, and then swung the game with a brutal offensive right at the end.

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Hmm, but y'know, maybe the match was already over from the moment they flipped the coin and determined that Kaeya would go second...

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: *sigh* I need a drink...

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Calm down, bro. Now's not the time to start drinking your sorrows away.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Knowing Captain Kaeya, he wouldn't want to see you upset over his loss.

dialogues.speaker: Mika
dialogues.text: Hey, why don't we learn how to play, too? Maybe then, we'll get to play against Captain Kaeya some day! Hehe... Though, I'm sure we'd lose pretty badly to him.

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Hah, yeah, you're right, Mika. Not a bad plan.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Hey there. Something else you wanted to discuss?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: The game's really caught on lately. It's a part of everyday life now — everywhere you go, you see people playing it.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: In fact, some people have even given up drinking in order to keep a clear head during the game.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Hehe, I'm sure Diona will be happy to hear that.

choices.text: How are the Knights of Favonius holding up?

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: I actually managed to convince Jean to join me for a game, but we only got part of the way through before she was called away. I ended up having to finish the match for the two of us. *sigh* What can you do? Everyone has to put their work first.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: But seeing how successful the tournament has turned out and how much fun everyone's had, I'm hoping that she at least has one less thing to worry about.

response.speaker: Kaeya
response.text: Sure. We should have a game of Genius Invokation TCG when you get the chance.

choices.text: How are the Knights of Favonius holding up?

dialogues.speaker: Eichendorff
dialogues.text: What an amazing tournament. That Timmie, huh... He really has a gift for this.

dialogues.speaker: Lennard
dialogues.text: Yeah, who saw that coming... But at least I can feel a little better about losing to him now.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: "City on the Lake Teems With Talent in TCG Tournament as Young Prodigy Bests Favonian Cavalry Captain"...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hmm, this title saves face for the Knights, but lacks a little "oomph"...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: "Top Strategic Mind of the Knights of Favonius Outsmarted by Bridge Boy in Five-Round Failure"...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: "Captain's Championship Hopes Crushed in Dazzling Dark Horse Defeat"...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hmm... Maybe I should stick with my first draft...?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: By the way, does Captain Beidou play Genius Invokation TCG, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Yes. In fact, she's one of the best in the whole Crux Fleet.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Would you mind putting in a word for me, Kazuha? I'm a long-time fan of Captain Beidou's. I've always hoped I'll get to make friends with her some day, but so far I've never had the chance.

dialogues.speaker: Kaedehara Kazuha
dialogues.text: Sure. But please be gentle when you inevitably defeat her in Genius Invokation.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: I've heard that even the unofficial Genius Invokation tournament is enjoying a huge turnout. Many serious TCG players have registered for both the official and unofficial ones.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: As for me... I don't mind trying my hand at the trending games from time to time, though I still prefer chess.

dialogues.speaker: Ningguang
dialogues.text: But when it comes down to it, whatever differences there may be between the various games around, they all share one important thing in common: They bring friends together.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hi there, my name's Charlotte. I'm a reporter for The Steambird.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Could I borrow a moment of your time for a brief interview?

dialogues.speaker: Brother Qian
dialogues.text: *sigh* Sure, go ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: You made a promising start in this competition, leaving many contenders in the dust on your way to the finals, before narrowly missing out on a championship win when you lost to Director Hu Tao of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. It must be difficult for you, knowing how close you came to victory.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: With this in mind, would you like to share your thoughts on how the final match played out?

dialogues.speaker: Brother Qian
dialogues.text: Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Brother Qian
dialogues.text: Sorry, do you want an answer for the media, or do you want my actual thoughts?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I'd like to hear your actual thoughts, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Brother Qian
dialogues.text: *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Brother Qian
dialogues.text: Well, I've always said that playing cards is seventy percent skill and thirty percent luck... But when your opponent rolls six dice of the same element at once, there's no coming back from that, not even with adeptus-level skills... so there was no hope for a mere adventurer like me.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Whew, that match between fox lady and fish lady really got my blood racing! The sweat's practically boiling off my forehead!

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Yes, yes. I'm sure all of Ritou knows how excited you are, but the gang's all waiting for us. We should be heading back now.

dialogues.speaker: Arataki Itto
dialogues.text: Ehh, they can wait a little longer... At least let my compadre and I play one last match! You can't say no to that... Pretty please?

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: That's my compadre! I knew you'd be down to duel! Only you understand a hardcore TCG player like me!

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Seriously, what will I do with you two...

response.speaker: Arataki Itto
response.text: It's okay, I don't blame you... But you should probably leave. You don't wanna see a grown oni cry...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: General Kujou, could I have a word with you?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Yes. Congratulations on your victory, Sangonomiya Kokomi.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: I wanted to express my gratitude for the helpful advice you provided before the match.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: It was nothing. Anyone with a good head on their shoulders knows that skill and strategy ultimately determine the winner. In any case, it was an exciting match to watch.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: It was unfortunate that you didn't register for the tournament as well.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I'd be no match for you.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Don't say that. You're not so different from me... seeking chances to hone your skills in the game, considering countermeasures, and competing with others as if they're friends.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: ...Perhaps you have a point.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: In that case, let's play a match of Genius Invokation before you depart from Narukami Island.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: It would be my pleasure.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I heard you refer to the opponent as a "kitsune youkai" earlier, could you tell me a little more about that?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Don't leave out any details. Who knows, maybe there's something I'll be able to use in my news piece.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Oh! I'd better not, I'm afraid of saying something wrong. Besides, I'm not really the most qualified youkai to answer questions.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Okay, then maybe you could help explain why a kitsune would have any interest in Fried Tofu.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Ah, now your questions are making me hungry.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Why don't I just take you to try some Kitsune Ramen here in Inazuma? I can explain while we eat.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: (I really didn't see that coming...)
